Reviewed partial outcome: **unsolved, 5/5**. The original quarter-filled optimal-flux problem allows arbitrary unit-modulus nearest-neighbor phases on large periodic square grids. Its global comparison remains unresolved. The finite setting here is explicitly even simple square tori of side at least four; finite-size and thermodynamic conclusions are distinguished.

The five verified results establish: torus gauge/plaquette constraints with both holonomies and a variational reduction, including the global four-by-four optimum and a distinct zero-flux tie; fourth/sixth moment identities and a strict improvement of the coarse global lower bound; the exact uniform quarter-flux spectrum and both optimal holonomies within that class for sides divisible by four; the complete eight-by-eight Hessian and strict local minimum modulo gauge; and existence of the all-even-size canonical energy-density limit with boundary and convexified all-rank block bounds. None establishes unrestricted quarter-flux optimality or a bulk counterexample.

Root checked all five written proofs and executable sources. Three distinct adversarial families and a fresh source-first whole-package reviewer reconstructed the mechanisms independently. The full128-by128 Hessian and all64 actual two-by-two Fourier blocks were reconstructed exactly; root reproduced the fresh programs and all16384 entries agree with the separately reproduced earlier derivation.
